config:
[nest]
name = "graph-allocations-nest"
chain = "arbitrum-one"
chain_id = 42161
rpc_urls = [
    "https://arb1.arbitrum.io/rpc",
    "https://arb-pokt.nodies.app",
]
schema_version = 1
block_timestamps = true

# EpochManager counts L1 blocks, and the log does not carry the L1 block. One row per block that
# carries a row of this nest; views/50-lodestar-epochs.sql places every epoch from it.
[extract]
l1_blocks = true

[[contracts]]
alias = "subgraph_service"
address = "0xb2bb92d0de618878e438b55d5846cfecd9301105"
start_block = 397492865
abi = "abis/subgraph-service.json"
events = [
    "AllocationCreated",
    "AllocationClosed",
    "AllocationResized",
    "LegacyAllocationMigrated",
    "IndexingRewardsCollected",
    "QueryFeesCollected",
    # `ServiceProviderRegistered` is the Horizon successor to `ServiceRegistry.ServiceRegistered`:
    # it carries the indexer's registration `data` blob rather than a `url`/`geohash` pair, so it
    # says an indexer exists on SubgraphService without saying where to reach it. The url and the
    # geohash still only come off the legacy `service_registry` contract below.
    "ServiceProviderRegistered",
]

[[contracts]]
alias = "curation"
address = "0x22d78fb4bc72e191c765807f8891b5e1785c8014"
start_block = 42449403
abi = "abis/curation.json"
events = [
    "Signalled",
    "Burned",
    # `Collected` is query fees paid into a deployment's curation pool. The subgraph's
    # `subgraphDeployment.signalledTokens` is deposits net of curation tax, less burns, **plus** these
    # collections - measured on five deployments against the subgraph (nuthatch#1078): the residual
    # after netting the tax was `curatorFeeRewards` to the wei on every one, and zero where no fee
    # had ever been collected. Without this event the fold is blind to it and reads low by up to
    # several percent on a deployment that has earned fees.
    "Collected",
]

[[contracts]]
alias = "epochs"
address = "0x5a843145c43d328b9bb7a4401d94918f131bb281"
start_block = 42449227
abi = "abis/epochs.json"
events = [
    "EpochRun",
    "EpochLengthUpdate",
]

[[contracts]]
alias = "disputes"
address = "0x2fe023a575449acb698648ed21276293fa176f96"
start_block = 397492858
abi = "abis/disputes.json"
events = [
    "IndexingDisputeCreated",
    "QueryDisputeCreated",
    "LegacyDisputeCreated",
    "DisputeAccepted",
    "DisputeRejected",
    "DisputeDrawn",
    "DisputeCancelled",
    "DisputeLinked",
]

[[contracts]]
alias = "escrow"
address = "0xf6fcc27aaf1fcd8b254498c9794451d82afc673e"
start_block = 397491106
abi = "abis/escrow.json"
# The escrow money movements Lodestar's `rav` module reads. `GraphDirectoryInitialized` and
# `Initialized` are deployment plumbing and deliberately left out.
events = ["Deposit", "Thaw", "CancelThaw", "Withdraw", "EscrowCollected"]

# The four Horizon delegation events Lodestar's feed already reads from graph-staking-nest.
# Declaring them here is what makes `views/80-lodestar-delegations.sql` true of *this* nest.
# Deploying this alongside graph-staking-nest indexes the same events twice; that is #1075's
# decision, not this view's. The allowlist is the same four events, nothing else.
[[contracts]]
alias = "staking"
address = "0x00669a4cf01450b64e8a2a20e9b1fcb71e61ef03"
start_block = 42449585
abi = "abis/staking.json"
# HEAD's four delegation events are the first four of the nine below - the wider list is what
# `network-snapshot` additionally needs, so this is a union rather than a replacement.
# What `network-snapshot` needs from staking: total staked, total delegated, and the distinct-address
# counts. Provisions are how Horizon expresses stake; delegation is its own pair.
events = [
    "HorizonStakeDeposited",
    "HorizonStakeWithdrawn",
    "ProvisionCreated",
    "ProvisionIncreased",
    "TokensDeprovisioned",
    "TokensDelegated",
    "TokensUndelegated",
    "DelegatedTokensWithdrawn",
    "StakeDelegatedWithdrawn",
    # Everything below is what an `indexer` entity needs and the two lists above do not carry
    # (nuthatch#1078). `lockedTokens` and `delegatedThawingTokens` are thaw state, and Horizon
    # expresses a thaw as a request rather than a balance, so the running total is the created
    # requests less the fulfilled ones - both the singular and the plural fulfilment event, because
    # a batched fulfilment does not emit the singular one. `provisionedTokens` needs
    # `ProvisionThawed` for the same reason. `indexingRewardCut` and `queryFeeCut` are
    # `DelegationFeeCutSet` in Horizon; `delegatorParameterCooldown` and
    # `lastDelegationParameterUpdate` have no Horizon equivalent at all and come only from the
    # legacy `DelegationParametersUpdated` below.
    "ThawRequestCreated",
    "ThawRequestFulfilled",
    "ThawRequestsFulfilled",
    "ProvisionThawed",
    "DelegationFeeCutSet",
    "OperatorSet",
    "HorizonStakeLocked",
    # The two slashing events. `ProvisionSlashed` has never fired (#1125); it is declared so that
    # the first one to fire is decoded rather than dropped, and `DelegationSlashed` alongside it
    # because a slash that reaches the delegation pool debits `delegatedTokens`, not `stakedTokens`.
    # `TokensToDelegationPoolAdded` is the credit in the other direction.
    "ProvisionSlashed",
    "DelegationSlashed",
    "TokensToDelegationPoolAdded",
]

# The same proxy address as `staking`, deliberately, and a second entry rather than a merged ABI.
#
# `0x00669a4c…` has had at least three implementations behind it. Horizon renamed the staking events
# wholesale - `StakeDeposited` became `HorizonStakeDeposited`, `StakeDelegated` became
# `TokensDelegated` - so the Horizon ABI describes only history after block ~408,847,369 and is
# silent about the 366 million blocks before it. Indexing only that half produced a
# `totalDelegatedTokens` that was *negative*: Horizon-era deposits minus legacy-era withdrawals.
#
# ABIs from Sourcify: the pre-Horizon implementation `0x0dae36ad…` for the stake events, and the
# StakingExtension `0x3be38557…` for `StakeDelegatedLocked`, because The Graph splits staking across
# a main contract and an extension that both emit from this one proxy.
#
# `StakeDelegatedWithdrawn` is deliberately absent here: its signature is unchanged across the
# upgrade, so the `staking` entry above already captures the whole of it, back to block 90,985,212.
# Declaring it twice would decode every log into two identically-populated tables.
[[contracts]]
alias = "staking_legacy"
address = "0x00669a4cf01450b64e8a2a20e9b1fcb71e61ef03"
start_block = 42449585
abi = "abis/staking-legacy.json"
# `StakeSlashed` is the reason this list is wider than the delegation view needed (#1125). The burn a
# dispute causes is `tokens - reward`: `reward` is the informer's share **of** the slash rather than an
# additional debit, so subtracting both double-counts. The check that catches over-subtraction is that
# no negative balance appears anywhere afterwards.
events = [
    "StakeDeposited",
    "StakeWithdrawn",
    "StakeDelegated",
    "StakeDelegatedLocked",
    # Slashing is the only other thing that reduces an indexer's stake, and it is why
    # `stakedIndexersCount` read 100 against the subgraph's 97 (#649 gap 3). Legacy only: 24 events,
    # 7 indexers, all before Horizon - `ProvisionSlashed` on the Horizon ABI has never fired.
    # Vendored by hand: the ABI Sourcify returns for this proxy is the StakingExtension, which does
    # not declare it. Shape confirmed against a real log rather than recalled - one indexed
    # `indexer`, then `tokens`/`reward`/`beneficiary`, with `reward` exactly half of `tokens`.
    "StakeSlashed",
    # The pre-Horizon half of the `indexer` entity (nuthatch#1078). Horizon carries none of this:
    # `DelegationParametersUpdated` is the only source of `delegatorParameterCooldown` and
    # `lastDelegationParameterUpdate` anywhere, and the legacy allocation lifecycle is where
    # `allocatedTokens` and `allocationCount` come from for every allocation opened before
    # SubgraphService existed at block 397,492,865.
    #
    # Two further implementations behind the same proxy, both read from Sourcify:
    # `0x2787f893…`, live at block 100,000,000, for the pre-exponential-rebates shapes, and
    # `0x0dae36ad…` (already named above) for what replaced them.
    "DelegationParametersUpdated",
    "AllocationCreated",
    # `AllocationClosed` is an *overload*, and both halves fired here. The 9-argument form carrying
    # `effectiveAllocation` ran from block 66,203,289 to 129,795,275 (7,564 logs); exponential
    # rebates dropped that argument and the 8-argument form has run since (over the 10,000 an
    # `eth_getLogs` sweep will return). Both are in the ABI, so nuthatch registers both and suffixes
    # the tables with the first two bytes of topic0: `staking_legacy__allocation_closed_7203` is the
    # 9-argument form, `staking_legacy__allocation_closed_f672` the 8-argument one. Declaring only
    # one would leave every allocation of the other era open forever, which inflates
    # `allocatedTokens` without ever correcting itself.
    "AllocationClosed",
    # Query fees, in the three shapes the contract has used. `AllocationCollected` (2,127 logs) and
    # `RebateClaimed` (2,227) are the pre-exponential-rebates pair and both stop at block ~129.9M;
    # `RebateCollected` replaced them. `queryFeesCollected` is the sum across all three.
    "AllocationCollected",
    "RebateClaimed",
    "RebateCollected",
    # `StakeLocked` is legacy `lockedTokens`, the thawing withdrawal the Horizon events express as
    # a thaw request instead. `SetOperator` and `SetRewardsDestination` are the legacy forms of
    # `OperatorSet` and of a rewards destination Horizon has no event for.
    "StakeLocked",
    "SetOperator",
    "SetRewardsDestination",
]

[[contracts]]
alias = "gns"
address = "0xec9a7fb6cbc2e41926127929c2dce6e9c5d33bec"
start_block = 42449510
abi = "abis/gns.json"
# Subgraph counts. `SubgraphPublished` is the universe; `SubgraphDeprecated` is what makes
# `activeSubgraphCount` different from `subgraphCount`.
# `curatorCount` is distinct addresses ever passed to `createOrLoadCurator` in the network subgraph
# (`helpers.ts:521`), and that is called from **eight** handlers, not one - `handleSignalled` and
# `handleBurned` on Curation, plus the V1 and V2 name-signal handlers on GNS. Most L2 signal is routed
# through GNS, so `L2Curation.Signalled.curator` holds the *GNS contract* rather than the person,
# which is why curating off Curation alone reported 50 against the gateway's 1,819. See issue #649.
events = [
    "SubgraphPublished",
    "SubgraphDeprecated",
    "SignalMinted",
    "SignalBurned",
    "GRTWithdrawn",
]

# `url` and `geoHash` on an `indexer` exist nowhere else on chain. Horizon's
# `ServiceProviderRegistered` carries an opaque `data` blob instead, so the legacy ServiceRegistry
# is still the only contract that says where an indexer can be reached. 394 `ServiceRegistered`
# logs from block 59,513,031 to 486,990,285, and 2 `ServiceUnregistered` - the pair is the whole
# lifecycle, and an unregistration is what makes a stale url disappear rather than persist.
#
# Address from `graphprotocol/contracts` `addresses.json`, key `42161`, contract `ServiceRegistry`.
# Start block by binary search on `eth_getCode`: empty at 42,449,356, 2,284 bytes at 42,449,357.
# One implementation ever - the proxy still points at `0xd32569da…`, the ABI vendored here - so
# unlike staking this needs no second entry.
[[contracts]]
alias = "service_registry"
address = "0x072884c745c0a23144753335776c99be22588f8a"
start_block = 42449357
abi = "abis/service-registry.json"
events = [
    "ServiceRegistered",
    "ServiceUnregistered",
]

# `rewardsEarned`. One alias rather than the two `staking` needed, because the rename here did not
# collide: `RewardsAssigned` became `HorizonRewardsAssigned` and both names survive in one ABI.
# `RewardsDenied` did not get renamed and *is* an overload - the legacy form carries `epoch` and the
# Horizon form does not - so nuthatch suffixes those two tables `_07b6` (legacy) and `_9b13`
# (Horizon). A denial is not a debit; it is why an allocation a caller expects to see rewards for
# has none, which is a question Lodestar gets asked and cannot currently answer.
#
# Address from `addresses.json` key `42161`, contract `RewardsManager`. Start block by binary search
# on `eth_getCode`: empty at 42,449,637, 2,284 bytes at 42,449,638. The ABI is hand-vendored from
# two Sourcify-verified implementations of this proxy, the same way `abis/staking-legacy.json` is:
# `0x5912afc5…`, live at block 400,000,000, for the legacy pair, and the current `0xa13cff50…` for
# the Horizon pair. The current implementation does not declare `RewardsAssigned` at all, so
# vendoring it alone would lose every reward assigned before block ~408,847,369.
[[contracts]]
alias = "rewards"
address = "0x971b9d3d0ae3eca029cab5ea1fb0f72c85e6a525"
start_block = 42449638
abi = "abis/rewards.json"
#
# `ParameterUpdated` is the fourth, and it is what makes the sampled `issuance_per_block` read below
# safe to take coarsely: the sample says what issuance *is*, the event says exactly which block it
# changed on. Its only parameter is the name of the parameter that moved, not its value, so it dates
# a change and never states one - the two are only useful together. Appended to the vendored ABI
# from the current implementation `0xa13cff50…`.
events = [
    "RewardsAssigned",
    "HorizonRewardsAssigned",
    "RewardsDenied",
    "RewardsDenylistUpdated",
    "ParameterUpdated",
]

# The collector, and the reason `lodestar_escrow_transactions` cannot carry an allocation for every
# row. 75 escrow collections have no matching SubgraphService fee event, and the network subgraph
# takes their `collectionId` from GraphTallyCollector's own `PaymentCollected` rather than from
# SubgraphService - so until the collector is indexed here, the RAV ingest has nothing to join those
# 75 on. `RAVCollected` alongside it because that is the receipt the collection was made against.
#
# ABI vendored verbatim from `/root/horizon-nest/abis/tally.json` on the Helsinki box, which has
# been indexing this contract since block 399,485,933 - one artefact, two nests, so a signature can
# never drift between them. It is a six-event trimmed file; the allowlist takes two of the six.
#
# The start block is **not** horizon-nest's. Binary search on `eth_getCode` puts deployment at
# 399,496,057 - empty at 399,496,056, 6,608 bytes at 399,496,057 - which is 10,124 blocks *after*
# what that nest pins. Nothing is lost by starting later: `eth_getLogs` over the whole gap,
# 399,485,933 to 399,496,056, returns zero logs of any topic from this address, which it must,
# because there is no code there to emit one. Not a proxy, unlike everything else here.
[[contracts]]
alias = "tally"
address = "0x8f69f5c07477ac46fbc491b1e6d91e2bb0111a9e"
start_block = 399496057
abi = "abis/tally.json"
events = [
    "PaymentCollected",
    "RAVCollected",
]

# The L2 GRT token, for `api/grt-flow`'s `totalGRTMinted` / `totalGRTBurned`.
#
# **`Transfer` is deliberately not indexed.** It is the whole GRT transfer stream on Arbitrum - tens
# of millions of rows - and the two numbers the route wants are the bridge flow, not the stream. The
# rewards-minting half of the subgraph's definition is `Transfer` from the zero address, which a nest
# cannot express as a filter today (`topics[1]`/`topics[2]` filters are not in the config surface),
# so indexing it would mean carrying the entire stream to fold two aggregates out of it. Out of
# scope here; `BridgeMinted` / `BridgeBurned` are the bridge flow exactly and cost nothing.
#
# Address from `addresses.json` key `42161`, contract `L2GraphToken`; implementation
# `0xaffcb961…`, ABI from Sourcify verbatim. Start block shared with `epochs`: the L2 protocol
# contracts went up in one deployment run around 42,449,2xx.
[[contracts]]
alias = "graph_token"
address = "0x9623063377ad1b27544c965ccd7342f7ea7e88c7"
start_block = 42449227
abi = "abis/graph-token.json"
events = [
    "BridgeMinted",
    "BridgeBurned",
]

# RFC-0023 tier 3. `network-snapshot` wants GRT `totalSupply`, and deriving it would mean indexing
# every L2GraphToken Transfer to sum mints minus burns - millions of rows for one number. A pinned
# read samples it instead, at a fraction of the cost, and stays deterministic because the block is
# pinned. Needs `--state-rpc`.
#
# Renamed from `grt_total_supply`, same cadence. One entry, not two - a second call to the same
# selector at a different cadence would be a strict subset of these blocks and pay for the same
# answer twice.
#
# The cadence stays at 100,000 because `/api/grt-flow` reads the *current* figure, which is always
# the newest sample; a finer grid buys resolution on history nothing asks for. At 1,000 the two calls
# below cost ~884,000 `eth_call`s across the backfill against ~9,000 here.
[[calls]]
name = "total_supply"
contract = "0x9623063377AD1B27544C965cCd7342f7EA7e88C7"
calldata = "0x18160ddd"
every = 100000

# `networkGRTIssuancePerBlock`, the same way. Selector is keccak256("issuancePerBlock()")[:4].
#
# Coarse on purpose, and this is the one where it costs nothing at all: `rewards__parameter_updated`
# dates every parameter change to the exact block, so the sample says what issuance *is* and the
# event says when it moved. A finer grid would state the same two facts more expensively.
#
# `start` is not the proxy's deployment block, because the getter is younger than the proxy: the
# call reverts at 75,279,039 and answers 0 at 75,279,040, found by binary search on the public
# archive endpoint. Sampling from the nest's start would buy 33,000 reverted rows and no fact. The
# earlier implementations expressed issuance as `issuanceRate()`, a per-block *ratio*, which is a
# different quantity and not what the route asks for.
[[calls]]
name = "issuance_per_block"
contract = "0x971B9d3d0Ae3ECa029CAB5eA1fB0F72c85e6a525"
calldata = "0x6c080f18"
every = 100000
start = 75279040

# Four governance parameters Lodestar's network page shows beside the aggregates, sampled the same way
# as supply and issuance (nuthatch#1160). Each is a getter on a Horizon-era contract, so `start` is the
# first Horizon block, 408,847,369; before it the getter does not exist and every row would be a revert.
# Values on 2026-09-05: delegation ratio 16, curation tax 10,000 PPM (1%), protocol payment cut
# 10,000 PPM (1%), max thawing period 2,419,200 s (28 days). The legacy `thawingPeriod`,
# `maxAllocationEpochs` and `delegationTaxPercentage` getters revert on the Horizon proxy and are not
# sampled: those parameters no longer exist, and the subgraph's values for them are frozen history.
[[calls]]
name = "delegation_ratio"
contract = "0xb2bb92d0de618878e438b55d5846cfecd9301105"
calldata = "0x1ebb7c30"
every = 100000
start = 408847369

[[calls]]
name = "curation_tax_percentage"
contract = "0x22d78fb4bc72e191c765807f8891b5e1785c8014"
calldata = "0xf115c427"
every = 100000

[[calls]]
name = "protocol_payment_cut"
contract = "0x7Aae8ae011927BC36Cb4d0d3e81f2E6E30daE06D"
calldata = "0x1d526e50"
every = 100000
start = 408847369

[[calls]]
name = "max_thawing_period"
contract = "0x00669a4cf01450b64e8a2a20e9b1fcb71e61ef03"
calldata = "0x39514ad2"
every = 100000
start = 408847369
